section_summary.extract_value: This section reports descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations for a single total sample (N = 369). It states that BMI correlated positively with body image discrepancy, cognitive fusion, and disordered eating, and was significantly and negatively associated with body appreciation (weak magnitude). The section notes strong associations between cognitive fusion and both body appreciation (negative) and EDE-Q (positive), and a strong negative association between body appreciation and disordered eating.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations for a single total sample (N = 369) presented in Table 1. Table 1 shows BMI mean = 23.21 (SD = 4.90) and intercorrelations among BMI, BID, CFQ-BI, BAS-2, and EDE-Q; the correlation between BMI and body appreciation (BAS-2) is r = -0.27 (p < .001). No country, age, gender-specific breakdowns, or recruitment/source information are reported in this section.
